biteOfDay: ing Recent reports from Table Rock show bass transitioning firmly into fall patterns, holding on long points, gravel roll-offs, and offshore structure in 20-40+ feet as they fatten for winter. Walleye and crappie are active around brush and points. On Taneycomo, rainbows remain plentiful with brown trout becoming more aggressive in the upper lake as water cools. Effective offerings include Berkley

tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~20 cfs at 10:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~20. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: With stronger generation this morning, focus on Taneycomo seams and current breaks with weighted rigs and 2-4 lb test. Drift a Berkley Pink PowerWorm, 1/16- to 1/8-oz marabou micro jig (black, sculpin, or olive with orange head), or a zebra midge under an indicator in the softer inside
